Chris Eperjesy
CFO, Custom Truck One Source
Yeah. Tami, the way I would think about it is it probably didn't come in as high versus our expectations as it did versus yours. That's why we've taken up the guidance, you know, the $20 million both on the bottom and the top end of the range. You know, I probably wouldn't add more than that in terms of what our expectations are for the balance of the year. You know, we've had two quarters in a row with record new equipment sales. Demand continues to be strong. You know, as we've talked about, inventory levels are in a very good position. We still have the demand, obviously. We, you know, we certainly expect to continue to see you know, pretty significant new equipment sales.
I would say the H1 of this year was a comp, you know, to last year, where we did have some of the challenges around inventory. Obviously the H2 of the year, last year, that started to loosen up some. We did have, you know, a pretty significant Q4.
Tami Zakaria
US Machinery Analyst, JPMorgan
Is it fair to say that your TES segment sales could have been higher, but probably supply chain kind of held it back versus your expectations?
Ryan McMonagle
CEO, Custom Truck One Source
Look, I think the supply chains continue to improve, right? I think that is why you see the Q1 on Q1, how significant the increase was in terms of new equipment sales Q1 on Q1. You know, we are seeing it improve. But yes, we're still seeing backlog build. You know, even to Mike's question before yours, Tami, at some point, you know, we would expect months on hand to start to decrease in terms of backlog. Yes, if there had been more supply chain, we would've been able to deliver more trucks. There's no question about that. But things are certainly looking up and are improving, which, you know, you're seeing in the results that we're reporting.
Tami Zakaria
US Machinery Analyst, JPMorgan
Okay, fantastic. Thank you.
Ryan McMonagle
CEO, Custom Truck One Source
Thanks, Tami.
Operator
The next question is from Justin Hauke of Robert W. Baird. Please go ahead.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Yeah, good evening, guys. Obviously, the revenue was really strong here. The ERS margin mix that you guys talked about, I don't know that everyone fully appreciates that, you know, that there's a sales component that runs through that and how sensitive your margins are to that. Maybe you could just give us some rough math on what the margin impact was from the sales being 45% of revenue in that segment versus kind of 36% last year, given that, you know, at least at a segment level, your margins in rental are like three times what they are in sales. I'm imagining that that, you know, really diluted the margins versus maybe a like for like basis.
Chris Eperjesy
CFO, Custom Truck One Source
Yeah, maybe I can expand a little bit on that. As we said in our introductory comments, the mix, Q1 this year versus Q1 last year shifted from 64/36 last year, so 64% for rental revenue and 36% for equipment sales. This year it was 55% and 45%. The margins are much higher on rental revenue versus equipment sales. You know, we mentioned that overall margins, adjusted gross profit came down from 58%–51% or just under 59%–51%. That was largely driven by that mix, 'cause you know, overall, we continue to see margins exactly where we expected them to be.
As we said at the end of last year, you know, a good guide for this year is, as we came out of the year, we felt like for the full year, we can exceed our segment margins for 2023 versus 2022.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Okay. I mean, yeah, just 'cause it's obviously we can't break that out, but it kind of sounds like maybe on a like for like basis, if you could break out the rental and the sales component of the ERS segment, the margins are maybe above what they would be last year, absent that issue. Would that be fair?
Chris Eperjesy
CFO, Custom Truck One Source
I would say they're consistent with where the margins were for the subsegments.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Okay.
Chris Eperjesy
CFO, Custom Truck One Source
You know, there could be some mix within each of those that could from quarter to quarter impact those margins.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Okay. Fair enough.
Ryan McMonagle
CEO, Custom Truck One Source
Justin, you also have to remember that the margin on the used equipment sales is so impacted by, you know, it's an accounting margin, so it depends on the age of what's being sold, and so it depends on, you know, how depreciated it is. That may shift quarter to quarter, depending on how the age of the equipment that's being sold within ERS.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Yeah, no, fair enough. I guess my second question is just as it relates to the guide, and obviously you don't give quarterly, but you'd kind of talked about going into this quarter that EBITDA growth was maybe, you know, would be in the mid-single digits. It was up 15%. Obviously it was strong in the first quarter. You talked about the mix for the year being 45/55 H1 versus H2 weighted in terms of the EBITDA. I guess if you do the math, at the midpoint of your guidance, that'd imply Q2 EBITDA at around $88 million. The Street numbers that are out there are around $97 million. I guess just maybe square that math and kind of what you're thinking about Q2 and the seasonality.
Chris Eperjesy
CFO, Custom Truck One Source
Yeah. You know, that could be a little bit narrower range in the 55/45 H2, 45 H1. The way I would look at it is there is some seasonality built into the quarters. We also, you know, just had two of the strongest quarters or the strongest quarters we've ever had in terms of rental asset sales, as well as new equipment sales. So there could be, you know, there's going to be some of that impact potentially in Q2. The way I would look at it is, you know, we'd expect, you know, high single digit, probably 10%-ish kind of range increase year over year from EBITDA, and would still expect that 55/45, maybe a little bit narrower than that, to hold.
Justin Hauke
Analyst, Robert W. Baird
Okay. Thanks very much.
Operator
There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the floor back over to Ryan McMonagle for closing comments.
Ryan McMonagle
CEO, Custom Truck One Source
Thanks. Thanks everyone for your time today and your interest in Custom Truck. We look forward to speaking with you on our next quarterly earnings call. In the meantime, please don't hesitate to reach out with any questions. Thank you again. Take care.
Operator
Ladies and gentlemen, that concludes today's conference. Thank you for joining us. You may now disconnect your lines.
